Compute replicate-aware barcode statistics

Source: R/gene_level_statistics.R
compute_barcode_statistics.Rd

Tests, for each barcode, the comparison given by the contrast with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFit, glmQLFTest). Unlike compute_metrics, which averages the replicates before computing the log2 fold change, this uses the variability between replicates: barcodes that are noisy across replicates get a smaller score. The score is reported as a signed Z-score (sign(Log2FC) * qnorm(1 - PValue / 2)), so that the table can be used with find_gene_zscore_hit and find_discordant_barcodes.

Usage

compute_barcode_statistics(screenR_Object, matrix_model, contrast)

Arguments

screenR_Object

The ScreenR object obtained using create_screenr_object.

matrix_model

The design matrix of the linear model, for example created with create_design_matrix (or with model.matrix).

contrast

The comparison to test: the name or index of a column of matrix_model, a numeric contrast vector (for example created with create_contrast) or a one-column matrix created with makeContrasts.

Value

A tibble with one row for each barcode and the columns Barcode, Gene, Log2FC, logCPM, F, PValue, FDR (Benjamini-Hochberg, over all the barcodes) and Zscore.

See also

compute_metrics, find_gene_zscore_hit, create_design_matrix, create_contrast

Examples

object <- get0("object", envir = asNamespace("ScreenR"))
design <- create_design_matrix(object)
contrast <- create_contrast(design,
    treatment = "Treated",
    control = "Control"
)
statistics <- compute_barcode_statistics(object, design, contrast)
head(statistics)
